subject: Architecture
title: The Pantheon: Rome's Perfect Circle
description: A 60-second lesson on The Pantheon: Rome's Perfect Circle.

hook.text: The Pantheon's dome has a 30-foot hole in the top. It was designed that way on purpose.

buildup.text: The oculus is the only source of light. Rain falls through it onto the gently sloped floor.

discovery.text: The dome's height and diameter are identical — 142 feet — creating a perfect sphere inside.

twist.text: It's nearly 2,000 years old and still the world's largest unreinforced concrete dome.

climax.text: Michelangelo called it 'the work of angels, not men.' He then based St. Peter's dome on it.

punchline.text: Two millennia later, nobody has built a bigger one without steel.

quiz.question: What is special about the Pantheon's dome dimensions?
options: It is the tallest dome ever constructed
Its height and diameter are identical, forming a perfect sphere
It is built entirely of marble blocks

details.summary: The Pantheon in Rome, rebuilt by Hadrian around 125 CE, features an unreinforced concrete dome 43.3 meters in diameter — still the world's largest after nearly 2,000 years.
details.whyItMatters: The Pantheon's dome remained the world's largest for over 1,300 years, proving that Roman concrete engineering surpassed anything built for more than a millennium afterward. Its interior perfection still inspires architects and awe.
takeaways: The unreinforced concrete dome spans 43.3 meters — a world record
A 9-meter oculus provides the only interior light source
The dome has stood for nearly 2,000 years without steel

faq.question: How does rain enter through the open oculus?
faq.answer: Rain does fall through the oculus onto the marble floor. The slightly convex floor has drain holes that channel water away. Surprisingly little rain enters because the building's thermal dynamics create an updraft of warm air that deflects light rain before it reaches the floor.

faq.question: Why hasn't the dome collapsed without reinforcement?
faq.answer: The dome uses progressively lighter concrete toward the top — heavy basalt aggregate at the base, lightweight pumice near the oculus. Coffered panels reduce weight. The 6-meter-thick walls at the base act as buttresses containing the dome's outward thrust.
